title: Media element load algorithm step 7.3 detaches the wrong MediaSource — the assigned media provider object has already been reassigned by then

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Step 7.3 of the [media element load algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#media-element-load-algorithm) is:

> 7. If the [media element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#media-element)’s [networkState](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-media-networkstate) is not set to [NETWORK_EMPTY](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-media-network_empty):
>     3. If the [media element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#media-element)’s [assigned media provider object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#assigned-media-provider-object) is a `MediaSource` object, then [detach](https://w3c.github.io/media-source/#mediasource-detach) it.

But the only thing which reaches that step with a `MediaSource` involved is the [`srcObject` setter](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-media-srcobject) — and that assigns **_before_** it loads:

> The `srcObject` setter steps are:
> 1. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)’s [assigned media provider object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#assigned-media-provider-object) to the given value.
> 2. Invoke [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)’s [media element load algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#media-element-load-algorithm).

So, by the time the load algorithm reaches step 7.3, the assigned media provider object is already the **_new_** value. Step 7.3 therefore never even sees the `MediaSource` that’s being replaced:

- `video.srcObject = anotherMediaSource`: Step 7.3 detaches the *incoming* `MediaSource`, which was never attached, and leaves the outgoing one attached.
- `video.srcObject = null`: Step 7.3 finds no `MediaSource` at all, so nothing’s detached.
- `video.load()` called directly: The assigned media-provider object is unchanged — so this is the one case where the step does what it reads like it should.

In the first two cases, the replaced `MediaSource` is never detached: Its `readyState` stays `"open"`, its `sourceBuffers` stay populated, and no `sourceclose` fires — even though the element it was attached to has been reset.

Note that MSE doesn’t describe the trigger this way. The note under [detaching from a media element](https://w3c.github.io/media-source/#mediasource-detach) says:

> _Going forward, this algorithm is intended to be externally called and run in any case where **the attached `MediaSource`, if any**, must be detached from the media element._

Once the setter has run, _“the attached MediaSource”_ isn’t the same thing as _“the assigned media provider object”_. MSE’s wording is the one that can be implemented; step 7.3’s cannot.

There’s another, separate reason step 7.3 is too narrow: A `MediaSource` can also be attached through a blob URL (`video.src = URL.createObjectURL(ms)`) — **which never sets the assigned media provider object at all**. So, even when reading step 7.3 at a point where the value hadn’t yet been reassigned, **it’d _still_ miss the most common way MSE is used.**

### Implementations

No engine keys detachment off the assigned media provider object; all track the attached `MediaSource` separately, and detach that.

- **Chromium** detaches from `HTMLMediaElement::ResetMediaPlayerAndMediaSource()`, driven by its own `media_source_attachment_` handle rather than by re-reading `srcObject`: [`html_media_element.cc`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/media/html_media_element.cc).
- **WebKit** keeps `m_mediaSource` on the element, clears it with `std::exchange` in `detachMediaSource()`: [`HTMLMediaElement.cpp`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLMediaElement.cpp)
- **Gecko** reaches `MediaSource::Detach()` through the decoder it owns, from `AbortExistingLoads()` -> `ShutdownDecoder()`: [`MediaSourceDecoder.cpp`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/media/mediasource/MediaSourceDecoder.cpp).

Ladybird has had to do the same — tracking the attached `MediaSource` on the element with an AD-HOC code comment explaining why step 7.3 as written isn’t usable: LadybirdBrowser/ladybird#10992.

### Imaginable fixes

- Have step 7.3 act on the `MediaSource` currently **attached** to the element, rather than the assigned media provider object — matching the wording MSE already uses. That’d need a term — since _“assigned media provider object”_ is the only handle the element currently has.
- Or reorder the `srcObject` setter so the load algorithm runs before the new value is assigned. That fixes the reassignment case — but not `srcObject = null`, and not blob-URL attachment.
- Or move the trigger out of the load algorithm entirely and let MSE own it, per its own note — that is, define detachment as happening whenever the element transitions to `NETWORK_EMPTY` (which is what the note already describes).

Related: w3c/media-source#378, on detaching not aborting a pending buffer append.
